title: Squeezed light from a semiconductor amplifier
authors: Andrey S. Aleksandrov, Anatoly V. Masalov
abstract: The possibility of generating light in a squeezed quantum state during saturated light amplification in a semiconductor amplifier is theoretically analyzed. Due to four-wave mixing process during amplification, weak components of the spontaneous emission of the medium with symmetric frequency shifts relative to the strong amplified wave acquire the quantum properties of two-mode squeezed light. The squeezing of quadrature components occurs in the range of frequency shifts of several GHz ($\sim$ the inverse relaxation time of the charge carrier density) and can reach 10 dB or more under optimal conditions. The formation of a two-mode squeezing phase facilitates the observation of the squeezing effect, in which a strong wave, playing the role of a local wave, exhibits quadrature noise suppression without additional homodyne detection.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates generating squeezed light using a semiconductor amplifier operating in a saturated regime. It shows that the four-wave mixing process generates two-mode squeezed light in sidebands around the main amplified wave. This effect is quantifiable and can reach significant squeezing levels, demonstrating a quantum nonlinear optical process in a solid-state device.
main_problem: The paper theoretically analyzes the generation of light in a squeezed quantum state when a semiconductor amplifier operates under saturated conditions.
main_result: The four-wave mixing process leads to the generation of two-mode squeezed light in sidebands around the strong amplified wave, with squeezing potentially reaching 10 dB or more.
method: The analysis involves solving coupled differential equations governing the light amplitude and carrier density, treating the side-band components as weak fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is a semiconductor amplifier medium. The model uses coupled rate equations for the carrier density and the light field amplitude, incorporating the four-wave mixing process.
key_observables: Quadrature noise suppression ($\langle\Delta E^2angle_{\min}$), energy gain of weak modes, and the degree of squeezing (measured in dB).
important_parameters: Henry factor ($\alpha$), input intensity ($S$), gain length ($Z$), and the characteristic frequency shift ($\Omega \sim 1/	au_e$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes weak fields for the side-band components and utilizes approximations derived from solving the coupled differential equations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mode spectrum showing the Bogatov effect and the relative energy gain of weak modes due to FWM for varying Henry factors ($\alpha$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by setting up the governing equations, deriving the relative amplitudes for side-bands, analyzing the energy gain via FWM, and finally quantifying the minimum noise fluctuation to determine the squeezing level.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (squeezing) with solid-state physics (semiconductor amplifiers), providing theoretical insights into non-linear quantum light generation in condensed matter systems.
